properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored CryptoJS surface inside the web3.js bundle compiled into geth's JS console (goja). RC4 is classically broken; it ships with the binary even though geth's Go code never invokes it. Changeable here only by rebundling/trimming web3.js or moving console deps upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped-library cipher surface in geth's JS console; 3DES is deprecated (112-bit effective security, quantum-relevant only via its 168-bit key — classical weakness dominates). Replaceable only by changing the vendored web3.js bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Engine-API (authrpc) posture decision: golang-jwt's built-in RegisteredClaims validation is disabled (WithoutClaimsValidation, node/jwt_handler.go:62) because it enforces iat<=now too strictly, then claims are checked manually — exp (optional), iat required and within ±60s (lines 69-76), per the execution-APIs spec. Signature verification and the HS256-only method allow-list remain enforced; iss/aud/nbf are not checked (spec-compliant). Deliberate and documented, not an open bypass — recorded as

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped-library MAC surface in the JS console; HMAC-MD5 is deprecated (MD5-based MACs). Only reachable from console JS, not from Go code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: THE core asset of this codebase: secp256k1 ECDSA/secp256k1 signatures and key pairs underpin every Ethereum account, transaction (crypto.Sign in crypto/crypto.go), devp2p node keys, RLPx handshake and ENR signing, plus the vendored libsecp256k1 C implementation in crypto/secp256k1. Quantum-vulnerable (Shor breaks ECDLP) — 'harvest now, decrypt later' applies to every signed transaction and exposed public key. Not changeable here: the algorithm is fixed by Ethereum consensus; migration to ML-DSA/

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture-control class: plain ==/!= comparisons flagged as non-constant-time. Sampled sites compare public consensus data (block/parent hashes), empty values and test expectations — not MACs or secrets — so practical timing exposure is minimal; real secret comparisons in crypto/ecies use subtle.ConstantTimeCompare (see ALG-36a15216). Kept as a posture observation, not an incident.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: math/rand (non-CSPRNG) used for test data, fuzzer input generation and tooling per the sample; all security-sensitive randomness in this codebase (keystore keys/IVs, JWT secrets, discv5 nonces) goes through crypto/rand (ALG-80605930). No secret generation observed on math/rand in sampled sites.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-CTR is the cipher mandated by the Web3 Secret Storage v3 keystore spec for encrypting account keys under a scrypt/PBKDF2-derived KEK; keystream is unauthenticated but the v3 format carries a Keccak-256 MAC over the ciphertext. Also covers the legacy presale-wallet CTR path. Spec-fixed; not changeable unilaterally.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two live AES-CBC uses: legacy presale-wallet import (AES-128-CBC decrypt of the encSeed under an EVP-BytesToKey-derived key — legacy compatibility path only) and the smartcard wallet secure channel (AES-128-CBC encryption plus CBC-MAC authentication in accounts/scwallet). CBC is unauthenticated by itself; the scwallet channel supplies a CBC-MAC, presale relies on a Keccak check.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same logical asset as ALG-710f61f0: these five sites are stdlib ECDSA operations (ecdsa.GenerateKey on crypto.S256()) grouped by the generic DSA rule — there is no finite-field DSA in this codebase. Key generation on secp256k1 for accounts and ECIES keys.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped-library MAC surface in the JS console; HMAC-SHA1 is deprecated for new designs. Not called by geth's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Engine-API (authrpc) JWT authentication uses HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) with a 256-bit shared secret supplied via --authrpc.jwtsecret / the jwtsecret file — mandated by the execution-APIs spec for the CL-EL channel. HMAC-SHA256 is symmetric: Shor does not apply, Grover only halves the 256-bit tag security; the secret is a bearer credential on localhost. Spec-fixed; not changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256r1 (NIST P-256) ECDSA verification exposed as EVM precompile 0x100 (RIP-7212), implemented in crypto/secp256r1 and dispatched at core/vm/contracts.go:1639; wycheproof test vectors in core/vm/testdata. Quantum-vulnerable ECDSA — Shor recovers the signer's key from signatures. Consensus-defined: replaceable only by protocol change, observable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go stdlib crypto/ecdsa — the account/signature layer of go-ethereum: key generation (accounts/keystore/key.go:155,167 via crypto.S256()), transaction signing via crypto.Sign, abi-bind transactors. All on the secp256k1 curve (S256()), so it is the stdlib face of the secp256k1 asset (ALG-673c8f24). Quantum-vulnerable ECDSA; migration is a consensus-level change, not fixable in this repo alone.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH key agreement over secp256k1: crypto/ecies implements ECIES (ECDH + X9.63 KDF + AES-CTR + HMAC) used by the devp2p RLPx handshake for peer session-key agreement, and the vendored libsecp256k1 ships its own ECDH module selected via CI build flags (cirrus.yml/ci.sh). Quantum-vulnerable: recorded RLPx handshakes can be decrypted later with Shor. Migration would need a protocol change to ML-KEM in devp2p.

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.25.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HTTPS client sessions using Go 1.25 crypto/tls defaults (module declares go 1.25.0). Go 1.25's default TLS config already offers hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 for TLS 1.3, so a capable server negotiates PQ key exchange; classical-only fallback (ECDHE) applies to older servers — harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure only in that fallback. Production site: the beacon light-client API fetcher (beacon/light/api/light_api.go, User-Agent go-https-client); remaining sites are rpc/devp2p tests.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signatures in crypto/signify — a minisign/signify implementation used to create and verify detached signatures over release artifacts and checksums during the build/release process (signs filedata and a comment). Quantum-vulnerable (Shor breaks EdDSA); release-signing key migration target: ML-DSA or SLH-DSA. Changeable here — it is geth's own build tooling.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture control (positive): the ECIES decrypt path verifies the message authentication tag with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare (crypto/ecies/ecies.go:325), avoiding a timing side channel on tag comparison. Inventoried as a posture artifact; no weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECIES parameter registry supports P-384 (AES192-SHA384) and P-521 (AES256-SHA512) variants in crypto/ecies/params.go:120+, exercised by the ecies curve test matrix; the curve actually used in production paths is secp256k1. Quantum-vulnerable NIST curves available in the shipped ECIES surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (original Keccak padding, not FIPS-202 SHA3) — the consensus hash of Ethereum: addresses, tx/block hashes, ABI selectors (accounts/abi/abi.go:251 revertSelector), Merkle-Patricia-Trie roots, EVM keccak precompile 0x01. Used in 173 files. Hash security under quantum attack degrades only via Grover (quadratic) — remains the strongest class in this codebase; algorithm fixed by consensus.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 as PRF/base for keystore and scwallet KDFs (PBKDF2-SHA256 in passphrase.go/presale.go, 50000-iteration pairing derivation in scwallet/securechannel.go:84), scwallet derivation-signature hash (wallet.go:73), beacon light-client SSZ/merkle hashing, and libsecp256k1 internal selftests. Not Shor-relevant (hash).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at three strengths: presale wallet import (accounts/keystore/presale.go:83 — 2000 iterations, password as its own salt, 16-byte AES key — legacy pyethsaletool compatibility, far below modern OWASP minimums), v1-keystore decryption (passphrase.go:346-352 — iteration count read from the JSON, legacy vectors ~2000), and scwallet pairing secret (securechannel.go:84 — 50000 iterations, 32 bytes). Legacy formats are fixed by compatibility; low presale/v1 iteration counts are the wea

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE2b: the vendored crypto/blake2b implementation backs EVM precompile 0x09 (BLAKE2b F compression function, core/vm/contracts.go:1028) — consensus-defined. Symmetric hash; Grover-only quantum impact; not changeable here (precompile spec).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES block-cipher instantiation sites feeding the concrete modes elsewhere in the inventory: keystore v3 AES-128-CTR key encryption (passphrase.go), presale wallet AES-128 (CTR/CBC), scwallet secure channel AES-128-CBC, discv5 v5wire AES (→GCM at crypto.go:156). All 128-bit keys derived from scrypt/PBKDF2 or session keys.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 is the keystore key-encryption cipher: aes-128-ctr in v3 keystores (declared and validated in passphrase.go:172/244), aes-128-cbc in the legacy v1 format fixtures. 128-bit keys derived from scrypt/PBKDF2; AES itself is not Shor-relevant (symmetric, Grover → 64-bit margin still acceptable). Spec-fixed by the keystore standard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the Web3 Secret Storage v3 KDF for account keys: geth encrypts new keystores with scryptN=2^18, r=8, p=1 (passphrase.go:145) and decrypts with JSON-declared parameters (passphrase.go:345); light-scrypt test vectors exercise the low-N variant. Memory-hard, not Shor-relevant (symmetric); parameters are standard-compliant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM in two live paths: discv5 v5wire packet encryption (NewGCMWithNonceSize + Seal/Open with keys from the HKDF handshake) and Clef signer's encrypted credential storage (signer/storage/aes_gcm_storage.go:152 with random nonce). Authenticated encryption — not Shor-relevant; healthy posture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256/384/512 family: scwallet BIP-32 master-key derivation (HMAC-SHA512, wallet.go:930) and the vendored CryptoJS HmacSHA256/384/512 helpers in the web3.js console bundle (internal/jsre/deps/web3.js:11220/11628/11952 — shipped library surface, no Go call site). Symmetric MACs — not Shor-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 derives discv5 session keys from the ephemeral pubkey + WHOAREYOU challenge (p2p/discover/v5wire/crypto.go:128 hkdf.New(hash, eph, challenge, info)); the cmd/keeper/go.mod line is an x/crypto sub-package note. Symmetric KDF — not Shor-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Integrity/governance artifacts: SHA-256 digest manifests for release binaries (build/checksums.txt, 78 entries) and era-file downloads (internal/era/eradl/checksums_mainnet.txt and checksums_sepolia.txt, 87 entries each) — used to verify downloads. SHA-256 digests; Grover-only quantum impact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: concatKDF (ANSI X9.63 KDF, SHA-256-based) in crypto/ecies/ecies.go:172 — derives ECIES symmetric keys from the secp256k1 ECDH shared secret; feeds the AES-CTR + HMAC used by the devp2p RLPx handshake. Symmetric KDF itself is not Shor-relevant, but its input secret is (ECDH).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-384/SHA-512: scwallet implements BIP-32 HD-wallet derivation with HMAC-SHA512 under the spec constant "Bitcoin seed" (accounts/scwallet/wallet.go:930) and uses SHA-512 in the smartcard secure channel (securechannel.go:154); ECIES P-384/P-521 variants declare SHA-384/SHA-512 MACs. Symmetric hashes — Grover-only quantum impact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256 in ECIES parameter sets: ECIES_AES256_SHA256 is the default secp256k1 parameter set (AES-256-CTR + HMAC-SHA-256) used to encrypt RLPx handshake auth messages; AES256_SHA384/SHA512 are the P-384/P-521 variants. Clef's aes_gcm_storage_test.go uses a hardcoded 32-byte key ("AES256Key-32Characters1234567890") — test-only material. Symmetric; not Shor-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/rand (system CSPRNG) across 62 files — the randomness source for keystore key generation and IVs, scwallet channel keys, discv5 nonces/ephemeral keys, etc. Healthy posture; no weak-RNG exposure in the sampled security paths.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWT signing capability declared in the module manifests: github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 v4.5.2 in go.mod (the live dependency — used by node/jwt_handler.go for engine-API auth) plus the dgrijalva/jwt-go module hash recorded in go.sum. This is the dependency-declaration face of the JWT assets ALG-c6eac685/ALG-07035178.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed key material: an RSA private-key PEM block (self-labeled "rsa-testing-key") embedded in two fuzz-corpus inputs under tests/fuzzers/txfetcher/corpus. Test material for the transaction-fetcher fuzzer, not a production secret — but it is committed key material and an inventory fact. Not changeable by rotation (it is fuzz input data).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto is the extended crypto provider for this build: main module uses pbkdf2, scrypt, hkdf, sha3, ripemd160 sub-packages directly (keystore, discv5, EVM ripemd precompile); cmd/keeper declares it too, and .golangci.yml references it. Post-quantum capability: none of the used sub-packages are PQ.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: DTLS library present as an indirect dependency (github.com/pion/dtls/v3 v3.1.5, go.mod) — a DTLS 1.2/1.3 implementation in the build graph; no direct import found in this tree (likely via pion/stun/WebRTC-related transitive path). DTLS key exchange (ECDHE-class) is quantum-vulnerable; capability ships with the module graph.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto declared in cmd/keeper/go.mod — the extended Go crypto library (scrypt/pbkdf2/hkdf/openpgp sub-packages are pulled into keeper's module graph as indirect requires). The library ships whatever algorithms the keeper module builds against; presence is the asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenPGP implementation available via golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp in cmd/keeper's module graph (indirect). x/crypto/openpgp is frozen/deprecated upstream (known weaknesses vs modern OpenPGP); included transitively by the keeper tool's dependencies. No direct call site in this tree — shipped-library surface only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed test key: cmd/geth/testdata/key.prv contains a 32-byte (256-bit) key blob — an secp256k1 private key used as geth test fixture for account import (algorithm not declared in the file itself). Test material on disk, not a production secret, but committed key material is an inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x/crypto/scrypt sub-package declared in cmd/keeper/go.mod (indirect) — memory-hard KDF capability in keeper's module graph; the main module uses scrypt directly for v3 keystores (see ALG-c1f8b585).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The JWT library actually used: github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 v4.5.2 (go.mod) — parses/validates engine-API HS256 tokens in node/jwt_handler.go. v4 line of the maintained golang-jwt fork; quantum impact only via its HMAC usage (Grover-halved, still 128-bit).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Abandoned JWT library recorded in go.sum (not a go.mod require): github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go is unmaintained since 2019 with known CVEs (aud-claim bypass CVE-2020-26160). Its hash sits in the module graph of this build; the live JWT code uses golang-jwt/jwt/v4 instead. Worth tracking for transitive exposure — a consumer of any dependency that still imports it would inherit the flaws.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x/crypto/pbkdf2 declared for cmd/keeper (indirect) — PBKDF2 capability in keeper's module graph; the main module uses it directly (keystore v1 decrypt, presale import, scwallet pairing — see ALG-4de3b020).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pion/dtls/v3 v3.1.5 declared in go.mod (indirect) — a DTLS 1.2/1.3 stack in the build graph. Its cipher/kex defaults are classically secure but not post-quantum (ECDHE/DTLS 1.3 groups); no direct import in the tree. Presence = capability shipped via the module graph.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: x/crypto/hkdf declared for cmd/keeper (indirect) — HKDF capability in keeper's module graph; the main module uses it directly in discv5 (see ALG-ab44ea08).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same asset as ALG-681ce0cd (OpenPGP declared in cmd/keeper/go.mod): the frozen x/crypto/openpgp package is in keeper's dependency graph — deprecated upstream, no application call site in this tree; recorded as the library-tier face of that algorithm-tier entry.
